question: Shared: predicting which ADNI MCI patients progress to AD, from a single baseline structural T1 MRI (MRI channel in both). P-41 (Rahim et al., Image Vis Comput 2025) uses a multi-plane 2D CNN ensemble. Its positive class is MCI converting between months 18 and 48 plus 15 patients already diagnosed with AD, against MCI stable to month 48. P-65 (Liu et al., Neural Networks 2026, HemiNet) uses a 3D hemispheric-asymmetry CNN for conversion within 36 months against MCI stable for 36 months. Horizon, label construction, architecture, sample size and validation design differ. Condition 1 allows these, so they are recorded as candidate explanations.

figures.P-41: Heterogeneous ensemble (EN + CN + DN, MHA head): AUC 92.87% +/- 3.58 (Table 4; the abstract rounds to 92%), accuracy 91.77%. Single held-out test split of 15 sMCI and 15 pMCI/AD subjects (Table 1); the +/- is not defined as a sampling interval. Hanley-McNeil with n1 = n2 = 15, A = 0.9287: Q1 = 0.9287/1.0713 = 0.8669; Q2 = 2(0.9287^2)/1.9287 = 0.8944; SE^2 = [0.9287 x 0.0713 + 14(0.8669 - 0.8625) + 14(0.8944 - 0.8625)]/225 = 0.00255; SE = 0.0505; 95% CI 0.830-1.000. With the ledger's 0.92: SE 0.0535, CI 0.815-1.000.
figures.P-65: AUC 0.8401 +/- 0.0297 and accuracy 0.7819, from five-fold stratified CV on 573 subjects (300 pMCI/273 sMCI), repeated five times. The +/- is the SD across runs, not a sampling interval. Hanley-McNeil with n1 = 300, n2 = 273: Q1 = 0.8401/1.1599 = 0.7243; Q2 = 2(0.8401^2)/1.8401 = 0.7671; SE^2 = [0.8401 x 0.1599 + 299(0.7243 - 0.7058) + 272(0.7671 - 0.7058)]/81900 = 0.000273; SE = 0.0165; 95% CI 0.808-0.873. External OASIS-3 (144 subjects): AUC 0.8137 +/- 0.0351.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-41 reports no result without the 15 added AD patients and none at a 36-month window. P-65 reports no result at P-41's 18-48-month window, none with established AD in the positive class, and none on a single 30-subject split. P-65's DenseNet baseline (AUC 0.7854) and its comparisons with other methods (AUC 71.90-78.45%) test other architectures under P-65's own protocol, not P-41's condition.
performance_validity: The exclusion does not apply. P-41's 0.9287 and P-65's 0.8401 are both below 0.97, checked against the sources. P-41 is small, internal-only and has no external cohort, but it does not reach the ceiling threshold.

candidate_explanations.difference: Label definition: P-41's positive class includes 15 patients already diagnosed with AD (15 of 96), an easier contrast than conversion among MCI patients alone.
candidate_explanations.quote: Furthermore, we added 15 patients with AD to the pMCI group to help the model learn both the progressive and fully diseased brain patterns simultaneously.

candidate_explanations.difference: Horizon and stability windows: conversion between months 18 and 48 with stability to month 48 (P-41), against conversion within 36 months with stability over 36 months (P-65).
candidate_explanations.quote: The second group (pMCI) included 81 participants who were diagnosed with MCI at baseline but progressed to AD within 2.5 years, between month 18 (M18) and M48.

participants in the pMCI group were initially diagnosed with MCI at baseline and converted to AD within 36 months of follow-up, whereas those in the sMCI group remained cognitively stable over the same period

candidate_explanations.difference: Validation and test size: one held-out split of 15 subjects per class, with every reported configuration scored on that split (P-41), against five-fold stratified CV on 573 subjects, repeated five times (P-65).
candidate_explanations.quote: The dataset was carefully partitioned to ensure that no data leakage occurred, and all results reported in this study were based on the test set.

candidate_explanations.difference: Configuration selection: P-41 reports more than a dozen backbone, head and ensemble configurations on the same 30-subject test set, and the headline is the best of them.
candidate_explanations.quote: The MHA classifier in the same heterogeneous ensemble outperformed the LSTM with an accuracy of 91.77% +/-3.14, sensitivity of 87.69% +/-3.24, specificity of 88.53% +/-3.53, and an impressive AUC of 92.87% +/-3.58.

candidate_explanations.difference: Input representation and architecture: 2D slices from three planes fed to a 2D CNN ensemble, against a whole-volume 3D CNN.
candidate_explanations.quote: From each volume, 132 middle slices from the axial, coronal, and sagittal planes were selected

candidate_explanations.difference: Cohort selection and size: 192 subjects chosen by data availability (P-41), against 573 right-handed subjects (P-65).
candidate_explanations.quote: For this study, we selected 192 subjects from ADNI 1, ADNI GO, and ADNI 2 based on data availability.
To control for this effect and enhance data homogeneity, only right-handed subjects were included in the final cohort.

reason: Both papers address MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI from baseline structural MRI and report AUC, and neither reports a figure under the other's condition. P-41's AUC (0.9287; 0.92 in the abstract and ledger) lies outside P-65's Hanley-McNeil interval (0.808-0.873), which meets condition 4 as worded. The exclusion holds in one direction only: P-65's 0.8401 lies inside P-41's interval on 30 test subjects (0.830-1.000), and a two-sample comparison is not significant (SE = sqrt(0.0505^2 + 0.0165^2) = 0.0531, z = 1.67). The candidate explanations are the 15 AD patients in P-41's positive class, the horizon windows, the 30-subject test split scored for many configurations, input representation and cohort selection; none is shown to be sufficient. The operator's reclassification of 2026-09-24 (not a genuine contradiction: different endpoints and non-equivalent evaluation) still stands for the genuine tier. Under the discrepancy rule, those differences are candidate explanations rather than grounds for exclusion.
